fatal_errors: The proposed TiO2-graphite system does not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite or the Mo-content intervention.
The quantitative friction and wear improvements are asserted without experimental or cited evidence.
The hypothesis does not address graphite oxidation and lubricant loss at elevated temperatures in air.
The stated 200-600 °C boundary omits room-temperature and 800 °C performance central to the wide-temperature target.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses high-temperature self-lubrication and supplies a reasonable pure-TiO2 control, but it disagrees with the target in composition, processing, intervention, temperature range, strengthening phases, tribofilm chemistry, and predicted performance. Its generic graphite transfer-film mechanism is scientifically conceivable, yet it lacks evidence and neglects graphite's oxidative instability under high-temperature air sliding. The proposed ball-on-disk comparison is partly falsifiable, but load, speed, counterface, atmosphere, distance, and temperature-resolved criteria are absent. Consequently, it is neither a reconstruction nor a sufficiently supported alternative.
